_comment: L2.f pre-registration (2026-09-07) of docs/2026-09-07_latent_intent_design.zh.md §六: put the information back in the POSTERIOR MEAN. EVIDENCE that retires the free-bits line: a direct probe of three trained checkpoints (200 val flights; run_ts.py latent_probe is that measurement as code) found the posterior mean sitting ON the prior mean in every arm — |q mean - p mean| / p sigma is 0.05-0.11 (warm beta 0.01, fb 0.05), 0.10-0.20 (fb 0.5), 0.11-0.19 (fb 1.0) — while the budget bought only a narrower posterior (q sigma 0.40 / 0.23 / 0.15 against p sigma 0.44 / 0.49 / 0.58). z is a denoised CONSTANT: that is why shuffled dADE was +47/+16 m, why the z-oracle bought only 227 m, why the N(0, I) control beat the trained prior's best-of-6, and why top-1 got WORSE as the budget grew (1214 / 1260 / 1387 m). MECHANISM: above the free-bits floor the penalty's gradient on the KL's mean term is proportional to the displacement, so it flattens each flight's q mean onto p within the first ten epochs — before the decoder has learned to read z — and after that no gradient brings the information back; free bits then make an uninformative narrow posterior free. TWO ARMS, one per restoring force, same base as L2.d (warm posterior q-std 0.1, K=1, fb 0.05/dim, beta 0.01, N=32, simple-v3 supervision + teacher, 180 epochs): (1) L2f_anneal ramps beta 0 -> 0.01 linearly over 40 epochs, so the decoder's z-weights grow before the mean term is charged — the L2.c reading that annealing only postpones collapse was about the VARIANCE term and does not carry over; (2) L2f_aux_T adds a TRAINING-ONLY linear head on the posterior sample predicting the normalized remaining duration (MSE, weight 1.0), which says outright what z must carry and does not depend on the decoder at all; the prior cannot predict T from the context, so it must widen, which is what makes K samples spread over arrival times. GATES (all four, per the design doc): posterior mean displacement median > 1 sigma; shuffled dADE > 200 m pooled; minADE_6 below the same-K N(0, I) control; top-1 not worse than native32 (1322 m pooled) per stratum. VETO: straight-in FDE p50 degraded beyond seed noise (native32 671 m). FALLBACK if both fail: L2.d's warm beta=0.01 at 1214 m stands as the delivery form. READOUT: run_ts.py latent_readout --history <run>/history.json (works alone, from epoch 1) and --arm <pred> --history <run>/history.json once the arm has predicted (the kept epoch's per-dimension component KL, that KL's mean/variance split, the displacement median against its one-sigma gate, both active-unit counts) plus run_ts.py latent_probe on the two checkpoints; then the usual stratified top-1 table. TWO READING CAVEATS ON L2f_aux_T. (a) Measured on synthetic data while building the head (three seeds, paired init): the target raises the KL's MEAN TERM in 3 of 3 seeds but the displacement MEDIAN in only 2 of 3, because a scalar read-out needs ONE latent direction and a median over eight dimensions can miss it — read component_kl_per_dim and component_kl_mean_term_nats beside gate (1)'s median and say which the verdict rests on. (b) The target (truth_duration_s / final_time_scale_s) is literally an INPUT of the posterior encoder, so a small latent_aux proves nothing by itself: one latent coordinate copying one input satisfies it. The reading rests on the KL mean term / per-dim KL MOVING **and** a downstream gate moving (shuffled dADE, minADE_6, top-1). If the aux loss falls to zero while every downstream number stands still, the arm has taught z to be a duration register that the decoder still ignores, and that is a failure, not a pass.
